# The Hound

Called Bramble; formal treaty-name Frithwed (D-0132). The fourth member of the
party — "the three plus the wolf spirit thing."

## The meeting and the name

> status: ratified (D-0132, D-0133)

The apprentice meets the hound caught in brambles and a hunting trap, and frees it.
The call-name Bramble grows from that moment; "drawing the thorn" (D-0116) is the
freeing itself, and the offered Frith-knot collar — with the formal name Frithwed —
seals what began there. A treaty that starts as a rescue, on the hound's terms.

## It exists and it counts

> status: ratified (D-0040, D-0064)

The author's phrasing places it inside the story's thesis: the central party — the
three plus the wolf-spirit — is the worked example of individual human agency bending
the cycle of history. The companion is not a mascot; it is one of the agents.

## Nature settled

> status: ratified (D-0116)

A Cù-Sìth/Gwyllgi moor-spirit, not a household dog — a minor landvættir in dog-shape, of the old animist order. It works only by consent. It understands a proof and
keeps its own silence — that silence two things at once, the reticence of a spirit and a Wyrd
fouled by a nearby mine's debt. The bond between it and the apprentice is a treaty: the
apprentice earns it by drawing the thorn and combing out the burrs, then seals it by offering —
the hound free to accept or refuse — a woven Frith-knot collar. Because it is a spirit, it can
outlive the trio and stand as the narrator-order's oldest witness ([[narrator]], D-0117). See [[animals]] for the wider rules.

## Proposed texture

> status: proposed

Unratified (the found-trapped meeting itself is now ratified — D-0133): bonded first
and closest to the apprentice; senses that read storms and patrols
before any human can; comprehension without speech; wary, formal respect toward the
protagonist — animals do not like how many people she smells like.
